This experiment needs WebGL.

Open it in a current version of Safari, Chrome or Firefox with graphics acceleration turned on.

Behind the image

What is calculated, and what is drawn.

Flat spacetime with no gravity. Light speed c = 1: distances are in light-seconds (ls) and times in seconds. The ship moves along x at speed v; its light clock’s mirrors are 0.5 ls apart across the direction of motion, so one tick (a round trip of the light) is 1 s of the ship’s own time. The ship is 4 ls long at rest.

Frames

“Seen from” picks the inertial frame used for every coordinate on screen. All events are computed once, in Earth’s frame, and then transformed exactly:

t′ = γ (t − v x), x′ = γ (x − v t), y′ = y, γ = 1 / √(1 − v²)

Switching frames animates through intermediate frames by changing the rapidity φ = artanh v smoothly, so every in-between picture is also a real frame.

Clocks

Each clock’s reading is its proper time, τ = ∫ √(1 − u²) dt along its worldline. The readout shows both clocks at the moment “now” of the chosen frame.

The flash

Light leaves the ship’s centre at ship time 4 s and reaches both ends 2 s later in the ship’s frame. In Earth’s frame the back is lit γ v L₀ earlier than the front. The expanding ring is the light, which is a circle around the emission point in every frame.

Length

A body’s length is the distance between its ends at the same time, in the frame doing the measuring: L = L₀ / γ along the motion. Distances across the motion do not change.

Round trip

The ship turns around instantly at Earth time 10 s (ship time 8 s at 0.6 c) and is home at 20 s, having aged 16 s. Real ships accelerate gradually; that changes the details at the turn, not the result. “Seen from: Ship, returning” uses the inertial frame of the return leg. During the turn itself the ship has no single inertial frame, so the ship’s body is drawn rigid within each leg.

Touch and keys

Drag to orbit, pinch or scroll to zoom. In Time view, hover or tap a tick mark or a flash event to see its coordinates in both frames. Keys: Space play/pause, ← → step, F switch frame, T Space/Time, R replay.

Invariants

The light cone (t² = x² + y²) and the curves t² − x² = constant are the same in every frame, so they stay still while events slide along them.

Drawn for clarity: the size of Earth (shown far too small to be to scale, but contracted correctly when it moves), its spin (tied to its own clock but sped up), the ship’s shape, glows and colours, and the 45° light cone (it relies on drawing 1 s of time and 1 ls of space at the same size). The view shows coordinates, not what a camera would see: light-travel delays, Doppler shifts and the visual rotation of fast objects are not rendered.
